title: Cap. X Arg. III close: reprobation does not fall on men only after they are considered to have persevered in sins to the last breath — many consequences of reprobation reach them in this life's course
pass_a_gloss: But yet more openly we confirm the Minor, namely, That reprobation does not fall upon men after they are considered to have persevered in their sins unto the last breath; Because many consequences of reprobation pertain unto the reprobate as constituted in the course of this life; such as are the denial of efficacious grace or of calling according to purpose, the permission of the wicked that they here go on in their sins unpunished, the delivering of the same unto a reprobate mind. These and other things of this sort.
pass_b_english: But we confirm the Minor still more openly: reprobation does not fall on men only after they are considered to have persevered in their sins to the last breath. Many consequences of reprobation belong to the reprobate while they are set in this life's course — denial of efficacious grace or of calling according to purpose; permission of the wicked to go on here in their sins unpunished; delivering them over to a reprobate mind. These and the like.
source_text: Sed adhuc apertius confirmamus Minorem, nempe, Reprobationem non cadere in homines postquam ad extremum halitum in peccatis suis perseverasse considerantur; Quia multa consequentia reprobationis pertinent ad reprobatos in hujus vitae cursu constitutos; qualia sunt negatio gratiae efficacis sive vocationis secundum propositum, permissio improborum ut impune pergant hic in peccatis suis, traditio eorundem in reprobum sensum. Haec et alia hujusmodi.
